sentences.zh: 孔崇弼，初仕後唐，自吏部郎中授給事中，時族兄昭序繇給事中改左常侍，兄弟同居門下，時論榮之。

translations.literal: Kong Chongbi, having first served Later Tang, was transferred from Bureau Director in the Ministry of Personnel to Supervising Secretary; at that time his clansman Zhao Xu moved from Supervising Secretary to Left Regular Attendant; the brothers both served together at the Gate, and contemporary opinion regarded it as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Chongbi began his career in Later Tang, rising from director in the Ministry of Personnel to supervising secretary. About then his kinsman Zhao Xu was shifted from the same supervising post to left regular attendant, so both brothers held office together at the imperial gate—a pairing that contemporaries hailed as a family distinction.

sentences.zh: 崇弼，天福中遷左散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Chongbi, during the Tianfu era was promoted to Left Dispersing Cavalry Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tianfu reign Chongbi was promoted to left dispersing-cavalry regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 無他才，但能談笑，戲玩人物，揚眉抵掌，取悅於人。

translations.literal: He had no other talent, but could only jest and laugh, play with people, raise his brows and clap his palms, to win others' pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed no other ability—only a gift for banter, for teasing others with lifted brows and clapping hands until his company was amused.

sentences.zh: 五年，詔令泛海使於杭越。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, an edict ordered him as maritime envoy to Hang and Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of the reign he was ordered by edict to sail as envoy to Hangzhou and the Yue region.

sentences.zh: 先是，浙中贈賄，每歲恒及萬緡，時議者曰：「孔常侍命奇薄，何消盈數，有命即無財，有財即無命。

translations.literal: Previously, gifts from Zhezhong each year constantly reached ten thousand strings of cash; commentators of the time said: "Supervisor Kong's fate is extraordinarily thin—how could he consume such a full sum? If there is fate there is no wealth; if there is wealth there is no fate."
translations.idiomatic: Envoys to Zhejiang had long returned with tribute worth ten thousand strings of cash a year, and wits remarked, "Regular Attendant Kong's fate is too thin for such a windfall—when he has luck he has no money, and when he has money he has no luck."

sentences.zh: 」明年使還，果海中船壞，空手而歸。

translations.literal: " The next year when the envoy returned, indeed the ship at sea was wrecked, and he returned empty-handed.
translations.idiomatic: " The following year the mission came home: his ship had indeed been lost at sea, and he returned with empty hands.

sentences.zh: （案：以下殘闕。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: the text below is defective.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: the remainder of this biography is missing from the source.)]

sentences.zh: 陳保極，閩中人也。

translations.literal: Chen Baoji was a man from Minzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Baoji came from Fujian.

sentences.zh: 好學，善屬文，後唐天成中擢進士第，秦王從榮聞其名，辟為從事。

translations.literal: He loved learning and was skilled at literary composition; in the Tiancheng era of Later Tang he passed the jinshi examination; the Prince of Qin Congrong heard his name and recruited him as a staff member.
translations.idiomatic: A scholar fond of letters, he took the jinshi degree in Later Tang's Tiancheng era. When Prince of Qin Li Congrong heard of him, he brought Baoji onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 從榮素急暴，後怒保極不告出遊宰相門，以馬箠鞭之，尋出為定州推官。

translations.literal: Congrong was by nature violent and impatient; later he grew angry that Baoji went out to visit the prime ministers' gates without informing him, and beat him with a horse whip; soon after he was sent out as investigating officer of Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Congrong was hot-tempered by nature. When Baoji slipped off to call on chief ministers without leave, the prince lashed him with a riding crop and soon had him posted away as legal officer in Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 從榮敗，執政知其屈，擢居三署，歷禮部、倉部員外郎。

translations.literal: When Congrong was defeated, the chief ministers knew he had been wronged and promoted him to the Three Bureaus, serving successively as Vice Director in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: After Congrong's fall the court recognized Baoji's mistreatment and moved him into the central secretariats, where he served as vice director in both the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，桑維翰登第之歲，保極時在秦王幕下，因戲謂同輩曰：「近知今歲有三個半人及第。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the year Sang Weihan passed the examination, Baoji was then on the Prince of Qin's staff and joked to his colleagues, saying: "I have just learned that this year three and a half men will pass."
translations.idiomatic: In the year Sang Weihan qualified for office, Baoji was still on the prince's staff and quipped to his fellows, "I hear three and a half men will pass the exams this year."

sentences.zh: 」蓋其年收四人，保極以維翰短陋，故謂之半人也。

translations.literal: " For that year four were admitted; Baoji, because Weihan was short and ugly, therefore called him half a man.
translations.idiomatic: " Four candidates were in fact chosen; because Weihan was squat and plain-looking, Baoji counted him as only half a man.

sentences.zh: 天福中，維翰既居相位，保極時在曹郎，慮除官差跌，心不自安，乃乞假南遊，將謀退跡。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, after Weihan had taken the chief ministership, Baoji was then a bureau officer and feared demotion or loss of rank; his heart was uneasy, so he requested leave to travel south, intending to withdraw from office.
translations.idiomatic: Once Weihan became chief minister in the Tianfu era, Baoji—still a bureau officer—feared a punitive transfer. Uneasy at court, he asked leave to tour the south and planned to retire from public life.

sentences.zh: 既而襄、鄧長吏以行止入奏，維翰乃奏於高祖曰：「保極閩人，多狡，恐逃入淮海。

translations.literal: Soon after, the senior officials of Xiang and Deng reported his movements to the throne; Weihan then memorialized to Gaozu, saying: "Baoji is a man of Min, very crafty, and I fear he may flee into the Huai-Hai region."
translations.idiomatic: Regional commissioners in Xiang and Deng soon reported his movements upstream. Weihan then told Emperor Gaozu, "Baoji is a Fujianese and notoriously slippery—I fear he will bolt into the Huai-Hai country."

sentences.zh: 」即以詔追赴闕，將下臺鍛成其事，同列李崧極言以解之，因令所司就所居鞫之，貶為衛尉寺丞，仍奪金紫。

translations.literal: " An edict at once recalled him to the capital; they were about to send him to the censorate to forge the case into a crime, but his colleague Li Song spoke strongly to clear him; therefore they ordered the relevant office to interrogate him at his residence, demoted him to Vice Director of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and still stripped his gold and purple.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict recalled him to the capital and the censorate nearly manufactured a capital charge, until colleague Li Song argued him free. He was tried at home instead, reduced to vice director of the imperial stud, and stripped of his gold-and-purple insignia.

sentences.zh: 尋復為倉部員外郎，竟以銜憤而卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored as Vice Director in the Ministry of Revenue, but in the end died nursing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon reappointed vice director of revenue, yet died still brooding over the affair.

sentences.zh: 保極無時才，有傲人之名，而性復鄙吝，所得利祿，未嘗奉身，但蔬食而已。

translations.literal: Baoji had no talent for his times and bore a reputation for arrogance; moreover his nature was mean and stingy—the salary and emoluments he received he never spent on himself, but ate only vegetables.
translations.idiomatic: Baoji lacked the gifts the age demanded and was known for haughtiness. He was also miserly: though he drew a full salary he lived on plain vegetables and spent nothing on himself.

sentences.zh: 每與人奕棋，敗則以手亂其局，蓋拒所賭金錢不欲償也。

translations.literal: Whenever he played chess with others, if he lost he would scramble the board with his hand—because he refused to pay the wagered money.
translations.idiomatic: When he lost at chess he would sweep the pieces off the board rather than pay his stakes.

sentences.zh: 及卒，室無妻兒，帷囊中貯白金十鋌，為他人所有，時甚嗤之。

translations.literal: When he died his household had no wife or children; in his curtain bag were stored ten ingots of white silver belonging to someone else, and people of the time greatly ridiculed him.
translations.idiomatic: He died without wife or child. In his travel bag were ten silver ingots that belonged to someone else—a detail that made him a laughingstock.

sentences.zh: 王瑜，其先范陽人也。

translations.literal: Wang Yu—his ancestors were from Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's family came from Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 父欽祚，仕至殿中監，出為義州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Qinhuo served up to Director of the Palace Domestic Service, then went out as prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qinhuo rose to director of the palace domestic service and later became prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 瑜性兇狡，然雋辯驍果，騎射刀筆之長，亦稱於當代。

translations.literal: Yu by nature was fierce and cunning, yet he was eloquent, brave, and sharp; his skill in riding, archery, and the brush was also praised in his generation.
translations.idiomatic: Yu was violent and treacherous by temperament, yet quick-witted, bold, and skilled in horsemanship, archery, and the written arts—talents admired in his day.

sentences.zh: 起家累為從事。

translations.literal: He began his career and repeatedly served as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service through successive staff appointments.

sentences.zh: 天福中，授左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: During Tianfu he was appointed Left Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianfu period he was made left guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 會濮郡秋稼豐衍，稅籍不均，命乘使車，按察定計。

translations.literal: It happened that in Pu prefecture the autumn harvest was abundant but tax registers were uneven; he was ordered to take the envoy's carriage and inspect and fix the assessment.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu's autumn harvest was rich but tax rolls were skewed, he was sent in the imperial inspector's carriage to audit and reset the levies.

sentences.zh: 既至郡，謂校簿吏胡蘊、惠鶚曰：「余食貧久矣，室無增資，為我致意縣宰，且求假貸。

translations.literal: After he reached the prefecture he said to the registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E: "I have been poor in food for a long; my household has no extra resources—pass word to the county magistrates for me and ask for loans."
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the prefecture he told registry clerks Hu Yun and Hui E, "I have been poor a long while and my house has no spare cash—tell the county magistrates I want a loan."

sentences.zh: 」由是濮之部內五邑令長共斂錢五十萬，私獻於瑜。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the five county magistrates within Pu's jurisdiction together collected five hundred thousand in cash and privately presented it to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: " The five magistrates under Pu thereupon pooled five hundred thousand cash and secretly gave it to Yu.

sentences.zh: 瑜即以書上奏，高祖覽章嘆曰：「廉直清慎有如此者，誠良臣也。

translations.literal: Yu at once submitted a memorial; Gaozu read the memorial and sighed, saying: "Integrity, uprightness, purity, and caution such as this—truly a fine minister."
translations.idiomatic: Yu immediately memorialized the court. Gaozu read his report and exclaimed, "Such integrity and sober caution—this is a true minister."

sentences.zh: 」於是二吏五宰即時停黜，擢瑜為太府少卿。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the two clerks and five magistrates were at once dismissed, and Yu was promoted to Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: " The two clerks and five magistrates were dismissed on the spot and Yu was promoted vice director of the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 杜重威之鎮東平也，瑜父欽祚為節度副使，及重威移鎮常山，瑜乃詭計於重威，使奏己為恒州節度副使，竟代其父位。

translations.literal: When Du Chongwei was stationed at Dongping, Yu's father Qinhuo was military deputy commissioner; when Chongwei moved his command to Changshan, Yu then used a deceitful scheme on Chongwei, making him memorialize to appoint Yu himself as military deputy commissioner of Hengzhou, and in the end replaced his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: While Du Chongwei governed Dongping, Qinhuo served as his deputy; when Chongwei transferred to Changshan, Yu tricked him into recommending Yu himself as Hengzhou deputy commissioner, supplanting his father.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，入為刑部郎中。

translations.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Bureau Director in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he entered the capital as bureau director of justice.

sentences.zh: 丙午歲，父欽祚刺舉義州，瑜歸寧至郡。

translations.literal: In the bingwu year his father Qinhuo was investigating commissioner of Yizhou; Yu returned home to pay respects and reached the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingwu year his father was censor-in-chief of Yizhou and Yu came home on family leave to the prefecture.

sentences.zh: 會契丹據有中夏，何建以秦州歸蜀，瑜說欽祚曰：「若不西走，當屬契丹矣！

translations.literal: It happened that the Khitan held the Central Plains; He Jian surrendered Qinzhou to Shu; Yu urged Qinhuo, saying: "If we do not flee west, we will belong to the Khitan!"
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then held the heartland; He Jian had surrendered Qinzhou to Shu. Yu urged Qinhuo, "Unless we flee west we will fall to the Khitan!"

sentences.zh: 」厲色數諫，其父怒而不從。

translations.literal: " With stern countenance he remonstrated repeatedly; his father grew angry and would not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " He argued again and again with fierce looks, but his father refused.

sentences.zh: 因其臥疾涉旬，瑜仗劍而脅之曰：「老懦無謀，欲趨炮烙。

translations.literal: Because his father lay ill for more than ten days, Yu took sword in hand and threatened him, saying: "Old coward without a plan—you wish to rush into the roasting pit.
translations.idiomatic: When his father lay ill ten days, Yu drew his sword and threatened him: "You old fool without a plan—you are marching into the fire."

sentences.zh: 不即為計，則死於刃下。

translations.literal: If you do not decide at once, you will die under the blade.
translations.idiomatic: Decide now or die on this blade."

sentences.zh: 」父不得已而聽之。

translations.literal: " His father had no choice but to obey.
translations.idiomatic: " His father had no choice but to agree.

sentences.zh: 時隴東屯兵扼其川路，將北趣蕃部假途，而因與郡盜酋長趙徽歃血為約，以兄事之。

translations.literal: At that time garrison troops in Longdong blocked their river route; they intended to go north toward the tribal lands to borrow a passage, and therefore with the bandit chieftain of the prefecture Zhao Hui made a blood oath as brothers, treating him as an elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Longdong troops blocked the river road, so they planned to borrow a northern route through tribal territory and swore brotherhood with local bandit chief Zhao Hui.

sentences.zh: 謂徽曰：「西至成都，余身為相，余父為將，爾當領一大郡，能遂行乎？

translations.literal: He said to Hui: "When we reach Chengdu in the west, I myself will be chief minister and my father a general—you shall command a great prefecture. Can you carry this out?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Hui, "In Chengdu I shall be chief minister, my father a general, and you shall hold a great commandery—will you see us through?"

sentences.zh: 」徽曰：「諾。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "Yes."
translations.idiomatic: " Hui answered, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 」瑜慮為所賣，先致其妻孥，館於郡中。

translations.literal: " Yu feared being betrayed and first sent his wife and children ahead, lodging them in the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: " Fearing betrayal, Yu sent his family ahead to lodge in the prefectural seat.

sentences.zh: 行有期矣，徽潛召其黨，伺於郊外。

translations.literal: The day of departure was set; Hui secretly summoned his followers and lay in wait outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: When the day came, Hui secretly gathered men and ambushed them beyond the walls.

sentences.zh: 子夜，瑜舉族行，輜重絡繹十有餘里。

translations.literal: At midnight Yu moved his entire clan; baggage and carts stretched in an unbroken line for more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight Yu set out with his whole clan, baggage wagons trailing for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 徽之所親，循溝澮而遁，至馬峽路隅，舉燧相應，其黨起於伏莽，斷欽祚之首，貫諸長矛。

translations.literal: Hui's intimates fled along ditches and streams; at a corner of the road at Maxia they raised beacon fires in answer; his party rose from ambush in the thickets, cut off Qinhuo's head, and threaded it on a long spear.
translations.idiomatic: Hui's men stole along irrigation ditches, lit signal fires at Maxia Pass, and sprang from the brush. They severed Qinhuo's head and ran it up a long spear.

sentences.zh: 平生聚蓄金幣萬計，皆為賊所掠，少長百口，殺之殆盡。

translations.literal: The gold and coin he had amassed in a lifetime, numbering in the tens of thousands, were all plundered by bandits; more than a hundred people young and old were killed, nearly all exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: A lifetime's hoard of gold—tens of thousands—was looted; of more than a hundred kin, young and old, nearly all were slaughtered.

sentences.zh: 瑜尚獨戰千人，矢不虛發，手無射捍，其指流血。

translations.literal: Yu still fought alone against a thousand men; his arrows never missed; his hands had no bow-grip left and his fingers bled.
translations.idiomatic: Yu alone fought a thousand men, every arrow finding its mark until his fingers, stripped of bow leather, ran with blood.

sentences.zh: 及窘，乃夜竄山谷，落發為僧。

translations.literal: When pressed, he fled by night into the mountains and valleys, shaved his head, and became a monk.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, he fled into the hills by night, shaved his head, and became a monk.

sentences.zh: 月餘，為樵人所獲，縶送岐州，為侯益所殺，時年三十九。

translations.literal: After more than a month he was seized by a woodcutter, bound and sent to Qizhou, and was killed by Hou Yi; he was then thirty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: A month later woodcutters seized him and sent him to Qizhou, where Hou Yi executed him. He was thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 始瑜有姑寡居，來歸其家，以前夫遺腹有子，經數年不產，每因事預告人吉兇，無不驗者。

translations.literal: Earlier Yu had an aunt living in widowhood who came to join his household; because her former husband's posthumous child was in her womb, for several years she did not give birth; whenever something occurred she would foretell people's fortune or misfortune, and none failed to come true.
translations.idiomatic: Yu had a widowed aunt who lived with him. She carried her late husband's posthumous child for years without delivering, yet foretold events for the household with unerring accuracy.

sentences.zh: 時契丹入中闕，前月餘謂瑜曰：「暴兵將至，宜速去之，茍不去，亂必及矣。

translations.literal: When the Khitan entered the central passes, more than a month before she told Yu: "Violent troops are about to arrive—you should flee quickly; if you do not flee, disorder will surely reach you."
translations.idiomatic: Before the Khitan entered the central passes she warned Yu a month ahead: "Violent soldiers are coming—leave at once or chaos will overtake you."

sentences.zh: 」後瑜果死，此謂「天作孽，猶可違；

translations.literal: " Later Yu indeed died; this is what is meant by "Heaven creates calamity, yet it may still be defied;
translations.idiomatic: " Yu died as foretold—illustrating the saying, "When Heaven sends disaster one may still resist it;

sentences.zh: 自作孽，不可逭」也。

translations.literal: When one creates calamity oneself, it cannot be escaped."
translations.idiomatic: but when one brings disaster on oneself, there is no escape."

sentences.zh: 張繼祚，故齊王全義之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Jizuo was the son of the former Prince of Qi Quan Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jizuo was a son of the former Prince of Qi, Zhang Quanyi.

sentences.zh: 始為河南府衙內指揮使，全義卒，除金吾將軍，旋授蔡州刺史，累官至檢校太保。

translations.literal: At first he was internal commander of Henan prefecture; when Quan Yi died he was appointed General of the Golden Wu, soon made prefect of Cai, and rose through offices to Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He began as internal commander of Henan; after Quanyi's death he became general of the golden guard, then prefect of Cai, rising to acting grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 明宗郊天，充供頓使，復除西衛上將軍。

translations.literal: When Mingzong performed the suburban sacrifice he served as provisioning commissioner and was again appointed general of the western guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Mingzong worshipped Heaven at the suburbs he directed supplies and was reappointed general of the western guard.

sentences.zh: 唐清泰末，丁母憂。

translations.literal: At the end of Tang Qingtai he entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Qingtai he went into mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 天福初，喪制未闋，會張從賓作亂，發兵迫脅，取赴河陽，令知留守事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, before mourning had ended, Zhang Congbin rebelled; troops were raised and he was compelled to go to Heyang and ordered to manage the regency.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianfu, while still in mourning, Zhang Congbin rebelled. Troops seized Jizuo, carried him to Heyang, and put him in charge of the regency.

sentences.zh: 從賓敗，與二子詔戮於市。

translations.literal: When Congbin was defeated, he and his two sons were executed by edict in the marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: When Congbin fell, Jizuo and his two sons were publicly executed by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 始繼祚與範延光有舊，嘗遣人以馬遺之。

translations.literal: Earlier Jizuo had been on good terms with Fan Yan'guang and once sent someone to present him with horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jizuo had been friendly with Fan Yan'guang and once sent him horses as a gift.

sentences.zh: 屬朝廷起兵，將討鄴城，為巡兵所獲，奏之，高祖深忌之。

translations.literal: Just then the court raised troops to attack Ye City; he was captured by patrol soldiers and reported; Gaozu deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: When the court marched on Ye City, patrols captured the messenger and reported it; Gaozu deeply distrusted Jizuo.

sentences.zh: 及敗，宰臣桑維翰以父珙早事齊王，奏欲雪之，高祖不允，

translations.literal: When they were defeated, the chief minister Sang Weihan, because his father Gong had long served the Prince of Qi, memorialized wishing to clear him, but Gaozu did not consent,
translations.idiomatic: After defeat Sang Weihan—whose father had long served the Prince of Qi—asked to clear Jizuo's name, but Gaozu refused,

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：史館修撰李濤上言：張全義有再造洛邑之功，乞免其族。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: Historiographer Li Tao memorialized: Zhang Quanyi had the merit of rebuilding Luoyang; I beg that his clan be spared.
translations.idiomatic: (From the Zizhi Tongjian: Historiographer Li Tao argued that Zhang Quanyi had rebuilt Luoyang and pleaded that his clan be spared.

sentences.zh: 遂止誅繼祚妻子。）〉

translations.literal: Therefore they stopped at executing Jizuo's wife and children.)]
translations.idiomatic: So only Jizuo's wife and children were spared from execution.)]

sentences.zh: 遂止罪繼祚一房，不累其族。

translations.literal: Therefore they stopped at punishing only Jizuo's household and did not implicate his clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the end only Jizuo's immediate household was punished, not the wider clan.

sentences.zh: 胡饒，大梁人也。

translations.literal: Hu Rao was a man of Daliang.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Rao was a native of Daliang (Kaifeng).

sentences.zh: 少事本鎮連帥為都吏，歷馬步都虞候。

translations.literal: In youth he served the military governor of his circuit as chief clerk and passed through the posts of cavalry and infantry commandant.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he served the circuit commander as chief clerk and rose through cavalry and infantry commandant posts.

sentences.zh: 會唐明宗鎮其地，與部將王建立相善，明宗即位，建立領常山，奏饒為真定少尹。

translations.literal: When Tang Mingzong was stationed there he was on good terms with the subordinate general Wang Jianli; when Mingzong took the throne, Jianli held Changshan and memorialized Rao as vice governor of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: When Mingzong governed the region Rao befriended Wang Jianli. After Mingzong's accession Jianli held Changshan and recommended Rao as vice governor of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 饒本憸人，既在府幕，無士君子之風。

translations.literal: Rao was by nature a slanderer; once in the prefectural staff he had none of a gentleman's bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Rao was a born slanderer and, once on the prefect's staff, showed none of a gentleman's conduct.

sentences.zh: 嘗因事趙郡，有平棘令張鵬者獻策，請建立於境內每縣所管鄉置鄉直一人，令月書縣令出入行止，饒乃導而薦焉。

translations.literal: Once when on business in Zhao commandery, the magistrate of Pingji Zhang Peng offered a plan, asking Jianli to place one village head in each village under every county in the territory, ordering monthly reports on the magistrate's comings and goings; Rao then guided and recommended it.
translations.idiomatic: On business in Zhao he met Pingji magistrate Zhang Peng, who proposed village informants in every township to log each magistrate's movements monthly. Rao championed the scheme to Jianli.

sentences.zh: 建立行之彌年，詞訟蜂起，四郡大擾。

translations.literal: Jianli carried it out for a full year; lawsuits swarmed like bees and the four prefectures were greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli enforced it a year; lawsuits swarmed and four prefectures fell into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 天成末，王都構亂，陰使結建立為兄弟之國。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiancheng Wang Du plotted rebellion and secretly sent envoys to bind Jianli as a brother state.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Tiancheng Wang Du rebelled and secretly offered Jianli alliance as an independent brother kingdom.

sentences.zh: 時饒又曾薦梁時右庶子張澄為判官，建立亦狎之。

translations.literal: At that time Rao had also once recommended Zhang Cheng of Liang times, former right attendant of the heir, as administrative aide; Jianli was also intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Rao had earlier recommended Zhang Cheng, a former Liang right attendant of the heir, as aide; Jianli favored him too.

sentences.zh: 澄素不知書，每座則以《陰府》、《鬼谷》為己任。

translations.literal: Cheng by nature did not know books; whenever he took a seat he made the Yin Fu and Guiguzi his own charge.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng could barely read; at every meeting he posed as master of the Yin Fu and Guiguzi.

sentences.zh: 建立時密以王都之盟告之，澄與饒俱贊成其事，會王師圍中山，其事遂寢，而饒之兇戾如此。

translations.literal: Jianli at times secretly told him of Wang Du's covenant; Cheng and Rao both approved the matter; it happened that imperial troops besieged Zhongshan and the affair then ceased—but Rao's ferocity was such as this.
translations.idiomatic: Jianli confided Wang Du's pact to him; Cheng and Rao both backed it until imperial troops besieged Zhongshan and the plot collapsed—yet this was Rao's vicious character.

sentences.zh: 清泰初，馮道出鎮同州，饒時為副使，道以重臣，稀於接洽，饒忿之，每乘酒於牙門詬道，道必延入，待以酒肴，致敬而退。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai Feng Dao went out to govern Tongzhou; Rao was then deputy commissioner; because Dao was a senior minister he rarely received him; Rao resented this and whenever drunk would curse Dao at the headquarters gate; Dao always invited him in, treated him with wine and food, and bowed as he withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Qingtai Feng Dao governed Tongzhou with Rao as deputy. Dao, a senior statesman, seldom saw him; Rao, drunk, would revile him at headquarters, yet Dao always welcomed him in, fed him wine and meat, and sent him off with courtesy.

sentences.zh: 道謂左右曰：「此人為不善，自當有報，吾何怒焉。

translations.literal: Dao said to those beside him: "This man does evil; he will have his own recompense—why should I be angry?"
translations.idiomatic: Dao told attendants, "He does wrong and will answer for it himself—why should I rage?"

sentences.zh: 」饒後閑居河陽。

translations.literal: " Later Rao lived in retirement at Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: " Rao later lived in retirement at Heyang.

sentences.zh: 天福二年夏，會張從賓作亂，饒謁於麾下，請預其行。

translations.literal: In the summer of the second year of Tianfu, when Zhang Congbin rebelled, Rao visited under his banner and asked to join the expedition.
translations.idiomatic: In summer of Tianfu year two, when Zhang Congbin rebelled, Rao sought him out and asked to march with him.

sentences.zh: 從賓敗，饒以王建立方鎮平盧，走投之，建立延入城，斬之以聞，聞者快焉。

translations.literal: When Congbin was defeated, Rao, because Wang Jianli was then military governor of Pinglu, fled to join him; Jianli welcomed him into the city, beheaded him and reported it—those who heard were pleased.
translations.idiomatic: When Congbin fell, Rao fled to Wang Jianli, now governor of Pinglu. Jianli admitted him, then beheaded him and reported the kill—a deed that gratified the realm.

sentences.zh: 劉遂清，字得一，青州北海人，梁開封尹鄩之猶子也。

translations.literal: Liu Suiqing, style Deyi, was a man of Beihai in Qingzhou, a nephew by marriage of Zheng, chief magistrate of Kaifeng under Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Suiqing, courtesy name Deyi, came from Beihai in Qingzhou and was related by marriage to Liang's Kaifeng chief magistrate Zheng.

sentences.zh: 父琪，以鴻臚卿致仕。

translations.literal: His father Qi retired as Director of the Court for Diplomatic Reception.
translations.idiomatic: His father Qi retired as director of the court for diplomatic reception.

sentences.zh: 遂清少敏惠，初仕梁為保鑾軍使，歷內諸司使，莊宗入汴，不改其職。

translations.literal: Suiqing in youth was clever; he first served Liang as commissioner of the Palace Guard, passed through the inner palace commissioners; when Zhuangzong entered Bian he did not change his post.
translations.idiomatic: Clever in youth, he entered Liang service as palace guard commissioner and inner-palace commissioner; when Zhuangzong took Bian his posts stood unchanged.

sentences.zh: 明宗即位，加檢校尚書僕射，委以西都監守。

translations.literal: When Mingzong took the throne he was given the acting title of Vice Director of the Secretariat and entrusted with guarding the western capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzong's accession he received an acting vice director title and was charged with guarding the western capital.

sentences.zh: 逾歲，以中山王都有不臣之跡，除遂清為易州刺史，俾遏其寇沖，既至郡，大有禦侮之略，境內賴焉。

translations.literal: After a year, because Wang Du of Zhongshan showed signs of disloyalty, Suiqing was appointed prefect of Yi to check his raiding thrust; once he reached the prefecture he had great strategies for defense, and the territory relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, with Wang Du of Zhongshan showing disloyalty, Suiqing was made prefect of Yi to block his raids. On arrival he devised strong defenses and the region depended on him.

sentences.zh: 王都平，加檢校司空，遷棣州刺史。

translations.literal: When Wang Du was pacified he was given the acting title of Minister of Works and moved to prefect of Di.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Du's defeat he received acting minister of works and became prefect of Di.

sentences.zh: 天成、長興中，歷典淄、興、登三郡，咸有善政。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng and Changxing he successively governed the three prefectures of Zi, Xing, and Deng, all with good administration.
translations.idiomatic: Through Tiancheng and Changxing he governed Zi, Xing, and Deng in turn, each with sound rule.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒潞王紀》：帝之起鳳翔也，召興州刺史劉遂清，遲疑不至。

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian, Annals of Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Prefect of Xing Liu Suiqing, who hesitated and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian, Annals of the Prince of Lu: When the emperor rose at Fengxiang he summoned Liu Suiqing, prefect of Xing, who delayed and did not come.

sentences.zh: 聞帝入洛，乃悉集三泉、西縣、金牛、桑林戍兵以歸，自散關以南，城鎮悉棄之，皆為蜀人所有。

translations.literal: Learning the emperor had entered Luoyang, he then gathered the garrison troops of Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and returned; from San Pass southward all towns and forts were abandoned and all fell into Shu hands.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing the emperor had entered Luoyang, he gathered garrisons at Sanquan, Xixian, Jinniu, and Sanglin and withdrew; south of San Pass every fort was abandoned to Shu.

sentences.zh: 入朝，帝欲治罪，以其能自歸，乃赦之。）〉

translations.literal: On entering court the emperor wished to punish him, but because he had been able to return of his own accord he was pardoned.)]
translations.idiomatic: At court the emperor meant to punish him, but pardoned him because he had come back of his own accord.)]

sentences.zh: 高祖即位之二年，授鳳州防禦使，加檢校司徒，會丁母憂，起復，授內客省使、右監門衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year after Gaozu's accession he was appointed Defender of Fengzhou, given the acting title of Minister of Works; he encountered mourning for his mother, was recalled from mourning, and appointed Commissioner of the Inner Guests and Grand General of the Right Gate Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Gaozu's second year he became defender of Fengzhou with acting minister of works. After his mother's death he was recalled from mourning as inner-guests commissioner and grand general of the right gate guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，駕幸鄴都，轉宣徽北院使兼判三司，加檢校太保。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, when the emperor visited Yedu, he was transferred to commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat with concurrent control of the three bureaus, and given the acting title of Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: In year six, when the court visited Yedu, he became northern palace secretariat commissioner with concurrent control of the three bureaus and acting grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 七年，少帝嗣位，加右領軍衛上將軍，仍賜竭誠翊戴保節功臣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Young Emperor succeeded, he was made general of the right leading army guard and still granted the merit title of Loyal and Diligent in Support and Preservation of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: In year seven, under the young emperor, he was made general of the right leading army guard and granted the merit title "Loyal and Diligent in Support and Preservation of the Realm."

sentences.zh: 八年，出領鄭州，加檢校太傅。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he went out to govern Zhengzhou and was given the acting title of Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he governed Zhengzhou with acting grand tutor rank.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，遷安州防禦使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun he was moved to Defender of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun year two he was transferred to defender of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 未幾，上表稱疾，詔許就便，回至上蔡，終於郵舍，時三年四月也。

translations.literal: Before long he memorialized illness; an edict permitted him to act as convenient; returning he reached Shangcai and died at a postal station—it was the fourth month of the third year.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he reported illness; the throne allowed him to retire where convenient. He reached Shangcai and died at a courier station in the fourth month of year three.

sentences.zh: 遂清性至孝，牧淄川日，自北海迎其母赴郡，母既及境，遂清奔馳路側，控轡行數十里，父老觀者如堵，當時榮之。

translations.literal: Suiqing by nature was extremely filial; on the day he governed Zichuan he himself went from Beihai to welcome his mother to the prefecture; when his mother had reached the border, Suiqing ran along the roadside, holding the reins and going several tens of li; the elders who watched were like a wall, and people of the time regarded it as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing was deeply filial. While governing Zichuan he rode from Beihai to meet his mother at the border, then walked her carriage reins in hand for miles as villagers lined the road—a scene men praised in his day.

sentences.zh: 遂清素不知書，但多計畫，判三司日，每給百官俸料，與判官議曰：「斯輩非盡有才能，多世祿之家，宜澄其汙而留其清者。

translations.literal: Suiqing by nature did not know books, but had many plans; on the days he adjudicated the three bureaus, whenever he issued officials' salaries he would discuss with the administrative aide, saying: "These people are not all capable—many are families of hereditary stipends; we should clarify the tainted and keep the pure."
translations.idiomatic: Suiqing was no scholar but full of schemes. When he ran the three bureaus and paid officials' salaries he told his aide, "Not all of these men are able—many hold hereditary stipends. We should sift out the corrupt and keep the upright."

sentences.zh: 」或對曰：「昔唐朝渾、郭、顏、段，每一赦出，以一子出身，率為常制，且延賞垂裕，為國美譚，未有因月給而欲沙汰，恐未當也。

translations.literal: Someone replied: "In Tang times Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan—each time an amnesty was issued one son entered service; that was the constant rule, and extending favor and leaving surplus was a beautiful talk of the state; there has never been wishing to sift because of monthly pay—perhaps it is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: Others answered, "In Tang, great houses like the Hun, Guo, Yan, and Duan clans won office for a son at every amnesty—that was custom and a national virtue. No one ever proposed purging the payroll; your plan may be wrong."

sentences.zh: 」群論由此減之。

translations.literal: Group discussion thereby reduced it.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly talked him down.

sentences.zh: 劉繼勛，衛州人也。

translations.literal: Liu Jixun was a man of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Jixun came from Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 唐天成中，高祖鎮鄴都，繼勛時為客將，高祖愛其端謹，籍其名於帳下，從歷數鎮。

translations.literal: During Tiancheng of Tang, Gaozu was stationed at Yedu; Jixun was then a guest officer; Gaozu loved his upright caution and registered his name in the roster, following through several commands.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang's Tiancheng era, when Gaozu governed Yedu, Jixun served as a guest officer. Gaozu admired his steady manner, kept him on the roster, and took him through successive postings.

sentences.zh: 及即位，擢為閣門使，出為淄州刺史，遷澶州防禦使，俄改鄭州，自宣徽北院使拜華州刺史。

translations.literal: When he took the throne he was promoted to Gate Commissioner, went out as prefect of Zi, moved to Defender of Cao, soon changed to Zhengzhou, and from northern palace secretariat commissioner was appointed prefect of Hua.
translations.idiomatic: On accession he became gate commissioner, then prefect of Zi, defender of Cao, and soon of Zheng; from northern palace secretariat commissioner he rose to prefect of Hua.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，鎮同州。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was stationed at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he governed Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 始少帝與契丹絕好，繼勛亦預其謀，及契丹主至闕，繼勛自鎮來朝，契丹責之。

translations.literal: At first when the Young Emperor broke with the Khitan, Jixun also took part in the plot; when the Khitan ruler reached the capital, Jixun came from his command to court and the Khitan reproached him.
translations.idiomatic: When the young emperor ruptured relations with the Khitan, Jixun helped plot it. When the Khitan emperor reached the capital Jixun came from his post and was rebuked.

sentences.zh: 時馮道在側，繼勛事急，指道曰：「少帝在鄴，道為首相，與景延廣謀議，遂致南北失歡。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Dao was at his side; Jixun in his urgency pointed at Dao and said: "When the Young Emperor was at Ye, Dao was chief minister and with Jing Yanguang plotted counsel, and thus north and south lost harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Dao stood nearby. In desperation Jixun pointed at him: "At Ye the young emperor had Dao as chief minister; Dao and Jing Yanguang schemed until north and south fell out."

sentences.zh: 臣位至卑，未嘗措言，今請問道，道細知之。

translations.literal: My rank was extremely low and I never put in a word; now I ask to question Dao—Dao knows the details."
translations.idiomatic: I was too low to speak. Ask Dao—he knows every detail."

sentences.zh: 」契丹主曰：「此老子不是好鬧人，無相牽引，皆爾輩為之。

translations.literal: The Khitan ruler said: "This old fellow is not one to make trouble—do not drag him in; you lot did it all."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan emperor said, "This old man is no troublemaker—do not drag him in. You people did this."

sentences.zh: 」繼勛不敢復對。

translations.literal: Jixun did not dare answer again.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun dared not reply.

sentences.zh: 繼勛時有疾，契丹主因令人候其疾狀，雲有風痹，契丹主曰：「北方地涼，居之此疾可愈。

translations.literal: Jixun then had an illness; the Khitan ruler therefore sent someone to inquire after his illness; it was said he had wind paralysis; the Khitan ruler said: "The northern land is cool—living there this illness can be cured."
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was ill; the Khitan sent to inquire and heard it was wind paralysis. The emperor said, "The north is cool—live there and the ailment will ease."

sentences.zh: 」乃命鎖繼勛。

translations.literal: " He then ordered Jixun locked up.
translations.idiomatic: " He had Jixun imprisoned.

sentences.zh: 尋解之，以疾終於家。

translations.literal: Soon he was released and died of illness at home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon released, he died at home of his illness.

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：契丹主聞趙在禮死，乃釋繼勛，繼勛憂憤而卒。）〉

translations.literal: (Zizhi Tongjian: When the Khitan ruler heard Zhao Zaili had died, he then released Jixun; Jixun died of worry and indignation.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Zizhi Tongjian: Learning Zhao Zaili was dead, the Khitan released Jixun, who died of grief and anger.)]

sentences.zh: 漢高祖入汴，贈太尉。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu entered Bian he was posthumously given Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Gaozu took Bian, Jixun was posthumously made grand preceptor.

sentences.zh: 鄭受益，

translations.literal: Zheng Shouyi,
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shouyi,

sentences.zh: （《新唐書·宰相世系表》：字謙光。）〉

translations.literal: (New Tang History, Tables of Chief Ministers and Clans: style Qian'guang.)]
translations.idiomatic: (New Tang History, Genealogy of Chief Ministers: courtesy name Qian'guang.)]

sentences.zh: 唐宰相餘慶之曾孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-grandson of Tang chief minister Yuqing.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-grandson of Tang chief minister Zheng Yuqing.

sentences.zh: 余慶生浣，浣生從讜，兩為太原節度使，再登相位。

translations.literal: Yuqing begot Huan; Huan begot Congyan, who twice was military commissioner of Taiyuan and twice reached the chief ministership.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's son Huan fathered Congyan, twice Taiyuan military commissioner and twice chief minister.

sentences.zh: 從讜兄處誨，為汴州節度使。

translations.literal: Congyan's elder brother Chuhui was military commissioner of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Congyan's elder brother Chuhui governed Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 家襲清儉，深有士風，中朝禮法，以鄭氏為甲。

translations.literal: The family inherited purity and frugality, with deep gentleman's bearing; court ritual and law took the Zheng clan as foremost.
translations.idiomatic: The clan lived in austerity with true scholar spirit; at court the Zhengs ranked first in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 處誨生受益。

translations.literal: Chuhui begot Shouyi.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhui was Shouyi's father.

sentences.zh: 受益亦以文學致身，累歷臺閣，自尚書郎遷右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Shouyi also entered office through literature, passing through the terrace and pavilion offices, from Secretariat Director promoted to Right Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: Shouyi too rose by letters, serving in central offices from secretariat director to right remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 天福七年夏，以張彥澤數為不道，上章請行國典，旬日不報。

translations.literal: In the summer of the seventh year of Tianfu, because Zhang Yanzhe repeatedly acted against propriety, he submitted a memorial requesting the national statutes be applied; ten days passed with no reply.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year seven, after Zhang Yanzhe's repeated outrages, he memorialized for statutory punishment; ten days brought no answer.

sentences.zh: 又貢表切言，訐直無所忌，執政稍惡之。

translations.literal: He again presented a memorial speaking sharply, impeaching directly without reserve; the chief ministers gradually disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: He filed again, blunt and fearless; the ministry grew to dislike him.

sentences.zh: 俄而以病請告，歸長安。

translations.literal: Soon he requested leave on grounds of illness and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he took sick leave and returned to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高祖晏駕，以不赴國哀停任，會赦，拜京兆少尹。

translations.literal: When Gaozu died he was suspended for not attending the national mourning; at an amnesty he was appointed Vice Magistrate of the Capital.
translations.idiomatic: For failing national mourning at Gaozu's death he was suspended, then after an amnesty made vice magistrate of the capital.

sentences.zh: 宰相趙瑩出鎮鹹秦，以受益朝班舊僚，眷待甚至。

translations.literal: When Chief Minister Zhao Ying went out to govern Xian and Qin he treated Shouyi, an old colleague of the court ranks, with the utmost regard.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Ying governed Xian-Qin he favored Shouyi, an old court colleague, with exceptional regard.

sentences.zh: 屬天下率借金谷，乃謂瑩曰：「京兆戶籍登耗，民力虛實，某備知之矣，品而定之，可使平允。

translations.literal: Just then the realm was levying grain and gold; he therefore said to Ying: "The capital household registers of increase and decrease, and the people's strength real or empty—I am thoroughly acquainted; grade and fix them and it can be made fair."
translations.idiomatic: The realm was levying grain and cash. Shouyi told Ying, "I know the capital registers and every household's means—let me grade them and the levy will be fair."

sentences.zh: 」瑩信之，因使與王人同掌其事。

translations.literal: Ying trusted him and therefore had him together with Wang Ren manage the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Ying trusted him and paired him with Wang Ren on the task.

sentences.zh: 受益既經廢棄，薄於仕宦，遂阿法射利，冀為生生之資；

translations.literal: Shouyi, having already been cast aside, was cold toward office; he therefore curried the law to shoot for profit, hoping for resources for daily living;
translations.idiomatic: Discarded once, he cared little for office and bent the law for profit to scrape a living;

sentences.zh: 又素恃門望，陵轢同幕，內奸外直，群情無相洽者。

translations.literal: moreover he always relied on his clan standing, bullied colleagues in the same office, inwardly treacherous and outwardly straight—among the crowd none were in harmony with him.
translations.idiomatic: and, leaning on pedigree, bullied fellow officials—outwardly upright, inwardly false—until no colleague would trust him.

sentences.zh: 及贓汙事發，騰於眾口，瑩不得已，遂按之，其直百萬。

translations.literal: When the corruption affair broke out it flew from everyone's mouth; Ying had no choice and therefore investigated; the straight value was a million.
translations.idiomatic: When bribery surfaced the scandal spread; Ying had to investigate and found a million in straight value.

sentences.zh: 八年冬，賜死於家。

translations.literal: In the winter of the eighth year he was granted death at home.
translations.idiomatic: In winter of year eight he was ordered to die at home.

sentences.zh: 受益數世公臺，一朝自棄，士君子皆惜之。

translations.literal: Shouyi's family for generations had been on the high terrace; in one morning he threw himself away—all gentlemen regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: Generations of his house had stood on the high terrace; in one morning he threw it away, and men of honor mourned it.

sentences.zh: 程遜，字浮休，壽春人。

translations.literal: Cheng Xun, style Fuxiu, was a man of Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Xun, courtesy name Fuxiu, came from Shouchun.

sentences.zh: （案：此下有闕文。）〉

translations.literal: (Note: text is missing below.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Editorial note: text missing below.)]

sentences.zh: 召入翰林充學士，自兵部侍郎承旨授太常卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned into the Hanlin as academician; from Vice Director of the Ministry of War as drafting commissioner he was appointed Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Summoned to the Hanlin as academician, he rose from vice minister of war as drafting commissioner to director of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 天福三年秋，命使吳越，

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year of Tianfu he was ordered as envoy to Wu and Yue,
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year three autumn he was ordered envoy to Wu-Yue,

sentences.zh: （《十國春秋》云：禮部尚書程遜為加恩使。）〉

translations.literal: (Ten Kingdoms Spring and Autumn states: Minister of Rites Cheng Xun was the favor-bestowing envoy.)]
translations.idiomatic: (Ten Kingdoms Spring and Autumn: Minister of Rites Cheng Xun served as favor-bestowing envoy.)]

sentences.zh: 母羸老雙瞽，遜未嘗白執政以辭之。

translations.literal: His mother was frail and aged and blind in both eyes; Xun never once informed the chief ministers to decline on that account.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was frail, elderly, and blind; Xun never asked the chief ministers to excuse him.

sentences.zh: 將行，母以手捫其面，號泣以送之。

translations.literal: When he was about to depart, his mother felt his face with her hand and wailed as she sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: As he left, his mother stroked his face and wept at the farewell.

sentences.zh: 仲秋之夕，陰暝如晦，遜嘗為詩曰：「幽室有時聞雁叫，空庭無路見蟾光。

translations.literal: On a mid-autumn evening the gloom was like pitch darkness; Xun had once written a poem saying: "In the dark chamber sometimes one hears geese cry; in the empty courtyard no road shows the moon's light."
translations.idiomatic: One mid-autumn night was dark as pitch. Xun had written, "Sometimes geese cry in the hidden room; no path in the empty court shows the moon."

sentences.zh: 」同僚見之，訝其詩語稍異。

translations.literal: " Colleagues who saw it were surprised that the poem's language was somewhat strange.
translations.idiomatic: " Colleagues who read it found the lines strangely ominous.

sentences.zh: 及使回，遭風水而溺焉。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he encountered wind and water and drowned.
translations.idiomatic: On the return journey wind and waves drowned him.

sentences.zh: 李郁，字文緯，唐之宗屬也。

translations.literal: Li Yu, style Wenwei, was a clansman of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yu, courtesy name Wenwei, was of Tang imperial kin.

sentences.zh: 少歷宗寺官，天成、長興中，累遷為宗正卿。

translations.literal: In youth he passed through offices of the clan temple; during Tiancheng and Changxing he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Imperial Clan Court.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he served the clan temple; through Tiancheng and Changxing he rose to director of the imperial clan court.

sentences.zh: 性平允，所歷無愛憎毀譽。

translations.literal: His nature was even and fair; in every post there was neither favor nor hatred, praise nor blame.
translations.idiomatic: Even-tempered, he inspired neither favor nor hatred, praise nor blame, in any post.

sentences.zh: 高祖登極，授光祿卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu ascended the throne he was appointed Director of the Court for the Imperial Brightness.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu took the throne he became director of the court for imperial brightness.

sentences.zh: 一日晝寢，夢食巨棗，覺而有疾，謂其親友曰：「嘗聞『棗』字重『來』，呼魂之象也。

translations.literal: One day he napped at noon, dreamed of eating huge jujubes, woke with illness, and told his kin and friends: "I have heard the character 'jujube' repeats 'come'—a sign of calling back the soul.
translations.idiomatic: One afternoon he napped, dreamed of eating huge jujubes, woke ill, and told friends, "The word for jujube echoes 'come'—a summons of the soul.

sentences.zh: 余神氣逼抑，將不免乎！

translations.literal: My spirit is pressed down—I fear I cannot escape!"
translations.idiomatic: My spirit is crushed—I may not escape!"

sentences.zh: 」天福五年夏卒。

translations.literal: " In the summer of the fifth year of Tianfu he died.
translations.idiomatic: " He died in summer of Tianfu year five.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made grand guardian of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 馬重績，字洞微。

translations.literal: Ma Zhongji, style Dongwei.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Zhongji, courtesy name Dongwei.

sentences.zh: 少學數術，明太一、五紀、八象、三統大歷，居於太原。

translations.literal: In youth he studied numerology, mastered the Great One, Five Records, Eight Images, and the Triple Concordance Great Calendar, and dwelt in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he studied numerology, mastering the Great One, Five Records, Eight Images, and Triple Concordance calendar, and lived in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 仕晉，拜太子右贊善大夫，遷司天監。

translations.literal: Serving Jin, he was appointed Right Guardian of the Heir Apparent of the Crown Prince, and moved to Director of the Astronomy Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he became right guardian of the heir apparent, then director of the astronomy bureau.

sentences.zh: 天福三年，重績上言：「歷象，王者所以正一氣之元，宣萬邦之命，而古今所記，考審多差。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianfu, Zhongji memorialized: "Calendars and celestial signs are what kings use to rectify the origin of the single qi and proclaim the mandate of the myriad states—but what ancient and modern records preserve, on examination, has many discrepancies.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu year three Zhongji wrote, "Calendars let kings fix the origin of cosmic order and proclaim the realm's mandate, yet records ancient and modern fail when tested.

sentences.zh: 《宣明》氣朔正而星度不驗，《崇元》五星得而歲差一日。

translations.literal: The Xuanding calendar's qi and new moon are correct but star degrees do not verify; the Chongyuan calendar gets the five planets but the year differs by a day.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanding calendar's solar terms and new moons are right but star positions fail; the Chongyuan gets the five planets but the year slips a day.

sentences.zh: 以《宣明》之氣朔，合《崇元》之五星，二歷相參，然後符合。

translations.literal: Taking the Xuanding calendar's qi and new moons and combining the Chongyuan calendar's five planets—when the two calendars are cross-checked, then they accord.
translations.idiomatic: Merge Xuanding's qi and new moons with Chongyuan's planetary tables and the two calendars align.

sentences.zh: 自前世諸歷，皆起天正十一月為歲首，用太古甲子為上元，積歲愈多，差闊愈甚。

translations.literal: From former ages every calendar began the year with the eleventh month of heavenly rectification, used the ancient jiazi as superior origin—years accumulated more and discrepancies grew wider.
translations.idiomatic: Older calendars began the year at the eleventh month and used the ancient jiazi era—errors widened as years piled up.

sentences.zh: 臣輒合二歷，創為新法，以唐天寶十四載乙未為上元，雨水正月中氣為氣首。

translations.literal: I have combined the two calendars and created a new method, taking the yiwei year of Tang Tianbao fourteen as superior origin and the mid-qi of the first month of Rain Water as the head of qi."
translations.idiomatic: I combined both into a new method: superior origin at Tang Tianbao 14 (yiwei), with Rain Water's mid-qi as the year's first term."

sentences.zh: 」詔下司天監趙仁琦、張文皓等考核得失，仁琦等言：「明年庚子正月朔，用重績歷考之，皆合無舛。

translations.literal: An edict sent down Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and others of the Astronomy Bureau to examine gains and losses; Renqi and others said: "On the first day of the first month of gengzi next year, tested by Zhongji's calendar, all accord without error."
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Zhao Renqi, Zhang Wenhao, and the astronomy bureau to test it. They reported the gengzi new year matched Zhongji's calendar without flaw.

sentences.zh: 」乃下詔班行之，號《調元曆》。

translations.literal: " An edict was then issued to promulgate it; it was titled the Tiaoyuan Calendar.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict promulgated it as the Tiaoyuan Calendar.

sentences.zh: 行之數歲輒差，遂不用。

translations.literal: After several years of use discrepancies appeared and it was then not used.
translations.idiomatic: Within years it drifted and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 重績又言：「漏刻之法，以中星考晝夜為一百刻，八刻六十分刻之二十為一時，時以四刻十分為正，此自古所用也。

translations.literal: Zhongji again said: "The method of clepsydra graduations takes the culminating star to examine day and night as one hundred graduations; eight graduations and sixty minute-graduations of twenty make one double-hour; the double-hour takes four graduations and ten minutes as correct—this is what antiquity used.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji also urged restoring clepsydra reckoning: one hundred day-night marks from the culminating star, eight marks and sixty sub-marks per double-hour, noon at four marks and ten minutes—as antiquity had it.

sentences.zh: 今失其傳，以午正為時始，下侵未四刻十分而為午，由是晝夜昏曉，皆失其正，請依古改正。

translations.literal: Now the transmission is lost; taking noon proper as the start of the double-hour, encroaching on the four graduations and ten minutes after noon as noon—thereby day, night, dusk, and dawn all lose correctness; I beg correction according to antiquity."
translations.idiomatic: " The art is lost: noon proper now starts the hour, swallowing the old measure, so day, night, and twilight are wrong. Restore the ancient rule."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 重績卒年六十四。

translations.literal: Zhongji died at the age of sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji died at sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 陳元，京兆人也。

translations.literal: Chen Yuan was a man of Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yuan came from Jingzhao (Chang'an).

sentences.zh: 家世為醫，初事河中王重榮。

translations.literal: His family for generations were physicians; at first he served Wang Chongrong of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: His family were physicians for generations; he first served Wang Chongrong at Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，後唐武皇自太原率師攻王行瑜，路出於蒲中，時元侍湯藥，武皇甚重之。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era the Martial Emperor of Later Tang led troops from Taiyuan to attack Wang Xingyu, the route passing through Puzhong; at that time Yuan attended with decoctions and medicines and the Martial Emperor greatly valued him.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianfu, when Later Tang's Martial Emperor marched from Taiyuan against Wang Xingyu through Pu, Yuan tended his medicines and won deep favor.

sentences.zh: 及還太原，日侍左右。

translations.literal: When he returned to Taiyuan he attended daily at the left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Taiyuan he attended the emperor daily.

sentences.zh: 武皇性剛暴，樂殺人，無敢言者。

translations.literal: The Martial Emperor by nature was fierce and violent, delighting in killing; none dared speak.
translations.idiomatic: The Martial Emperor was brutal and bloodthirsty; none dared remonstrate.

sentences.zh: 元深測其情，每有暴怒，則從容啟諫，免禍者不一，以是晉人深德之，勛貴賂遺盈門。

translations.literal: Yuan deeply gauged his feelings; whenever there was violent rage he would calmly open remonstrance—those spared from calamity were not one or two; therefore the people of Jin deeply thanked him, and the meritorious and noble bribed and gifted until his gates overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan read his moods; at each rage he pleaded calmly and saved many lives. Jin's nobles heaped gifts on his door in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 性好酒樂施，隨得而無私積。

translations.literal: His nature loved wine and he delighted in giving; whatever he gained he had no private hoard.
translations.idiomatic: He loved wine and lavished gifts, keeping nothing for himself.

sentences.zh: 明宗朝，為太原少尹，入為太府卿。

translations.literal: In the Mingzong reign he was Vice Magistrate of Taiyuan and entered the capital as Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mingzong he was Taiyuan vice magistrate, then entered the capital as director of the imperial treasury.

sentences.zh: 長興中，集平生所驗方七十五首，並修合藥法百件，號曰《要術》，刊石置於太原府衙門之左，以示於眾，病者賴焉。

translations.literal: During Changxing he collected seventy-five prescriptions he had verified in life and also a hundred items of compounding methods, titled Essential Methods, carved in stone and set to the left of the gate of the Taiyuan prefectural headquarters to show the multitude; the sick relied on it.
translations.idiomatic: In Changxing he compiled seventy-five proven prescriptions and a hundred compound formulas as Essential Methods, carved them on stone left of Taiyuan's prefectural gate, and the sick benefited.

sentences.zh: 天福中，以耄期上表求退，以光祿卿致仕，卒於晉陽，年八十餘。

translations.literal: During Tianfu, because of advanced age he submitted a memorial requesting retirement and retired as Director of the Court for Imperial Brightness; he died at Jinyang at more than eighty years.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu, aged, he sought retirement, retired as director of imperial brightness, and died at Jinyang past eighty.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：夫彰善癉惡，《麟史》之為義也；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: To display good and suppress evil is the meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: To honor good and condemn evil is the Spring and Autumn's purpose;

sentences.zh: 瑜不掩瑕，虹玉之為德也。

translations.literal: not to cover flaws is the virtue of rainbow jade.
translations.idiomatic: and not to hide flaws is the virtue of rainbow jade.

sentences.zh: 故自崇弼而下，善者既書之，其不善者亦書之，庶使後之君子見善如不及，見惡如探湯也。

translations.literal: Therefore from Chongbi downward, what was good has been written, and what was not good has also been written—so that later gentlemen may see good as if unable to reach it, and see evil as if plunging the hand into boiling water.
translations.idiomatic: From Chongbi onward we record both virtue and vice so later gentlemen may rush toward good yet shrink from evil as from boiling water.

sentences.zh: 至如重績之曆法，陳元之醫道，亦不可漏其名而弗紀也。

translations.literal: As for Zhongji's calendrical method and Yuan's medical way, one also cannot omit their names and fail to record them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongji's calendar and Yuan's medicine likewise deserve names in this record.
